title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering

key_results: Best Strict Success Rate of 24.69% on full tasks; paired inference cost reduction averages 64.4%; Type II ranking correlation with full tasks (ρ=0.9747)

title: Evaluating foundation models on official German medical licensing examinations: Implications for high-stakes assessment and AI-assisted medical education
task: Evaluating foundation models on German medical licensing examinations for high-stakes assessment
key_results: Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved 99.31% accuracy (M1) and 98.37% (M2); proprietary frontier models near-ceiling; open-weight models (GLM-5, DeepSeek V3.2-Thinking) competitive; compact models exceeded mean student performance; image-present items showed disproportionate difficulty for models versus students.
comments: Rigorous evaluation on restricted-access official benchmark demonstrates rapid frontier model progress, though the disproportionate model difficulty on multimodal items highlights residual visual reasoning gaps relevant to clinical practice.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Proprietary frontier models achieve near-ceiling performance on medical licensing examinations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Gemini 3.1 Pro 99.31% (M1), 98.37% (M2)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Open-weight models are competitive with proprietary systems on text-only subset
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: GLM-5 and DeepSeek V3.2-Thinking performed highly competitively

hypotheses.hypothesis: Image-present items are disproportionately difficult for models relative to students
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: larger performance decline for models than students on multimodal items

title: Mapping structural aging across human tissues reveals tissue-specific trajectories and coordinated deterioration
task: Quantifying structural aging across human tissues from histopathology images
key_results: Identified nonlinear, tissue-specific aging trajectories across 40 tissues; vascular tissue accelerates early, uterus/vagina accelerate around menopause; coordinated deterioration linked by sex hormones.
comments: PathStAR's approach of learning tissue structure without explicit age training is elegant, though validation of causality versus correlation in cross-organ deterioration patterns would strengthen claims.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Organ structural aging follows distinct nonlinear trajectories specific to tissue type
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: vascular early acceleration, reproductive late acceleration, biphasic patterns in digestive/male reproductive organs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structural aging characterized by inflammation and metabolic suppression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across organs showing coordinated deterioration

title: Peripheral blood microarray-based transcriptomic and epigenetic analyses identify immune, inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation in Alzheimer’s disease
task: Multi-omics transcriptomic and epigenetic profiling of peripheral blood to identify AD molecular signatures
key_results: Peripheral transcriptome (N=669) and epigenome (N=553) identified dysregulated genes (MAPK14, GM2A, CD177) and co-expression networks; strong APOE ε4 influence; immune activation, inflammation, metabolic suppression; MXD3 and NR4A1 protective against MCI-to-AD progression.
comments: Well-powered multi-omics study linking peripheral signatures to central pathology (amyloid, p-tau, NfL, atrophy), though peripheral biomarkers may not directly reflect brain pathology mechanisms.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Peripheral immune activation, inflammation, and metabolic suppression characterize AD pathophysiology
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: consistent transcriptomic patterns with strong APOE ε4 influence

hypotheses.hypothesis: MXD3 and NR4A1 expression levels predict protection against MCI-to-AD progression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: identified as protective genes in progression analysis

title: Multi-modal learning with incomplete data
task: Unified Python package for incomplete multimodal data integration and analysis
key_results: iMML package released with diverse use cases in biomedicine, text, and vision; versatile methods for missing modalities
comments: Software contribution with broad applicability; specific quantitative benchmarks not provided in abstract.

title: Predicting ionic conductivity of sulfide glass solid-state electrolytes using max-flow methodology
task: Ionic conductivity prediction for sulfide glass electrolytes via max-flow topology analysis
key_results: Positive correlation between max-flow and simulated ionic conductivity; method valid for high-conductivity sulfide glasses; static structure prediction feasible
comments: Max-flow as surrogate for ion transport in disordered materials is conceptually novel; relies on MD-validated correlations; acceleration of discovery demonstrated in principle.

model_io.model: Max-flow algorithm on periodic boundary graph

hypotheses.hypothesis: Topological max-flow from static structure predicts ionic conductivity without dynamic simulation
hypotheses.result: Supported for high-conductivity sulfide glasses; correlation demonstrated

title: A temporal graph attention autoencoder framework quantifies geopolitical trade risk through the evolutionary embedding of international trade networks
task: Geopolitical trade risk quantification via temporal graph embedding and evolutionary network analysis
key_results: Link prediction AUC = 0.932; GTRI captures 2014 Crimea and 2022 Russia–Ukraine disruptions; Granger causality confirms GTRI predictive content for GPR index
comments: TGAA model avoids over-smoothing via residual connections; entropy-weighted risk index is data-driven; sensitivity tests validate robustness but generalization to non-trade networks unclear.

inputs: UN Comtrade bilateral trade flows, 178 countries, 2001–2023

hypotheses.hypothesis: Network-embedding-derived structural signals encode forward-looking information about geopolitical tensions beyond text-based indices
hypotheses.result: Supported by Augmented Toda–Yamamoto Granger causality and effective transfer entropy tests

title: Multiscale patterns of migration flows in Austria: regionalization, administrative barriers, and urban-rural divides
task: Internal migration pattern analysis via network methods and regionalization
key_results: Significant deviations from gravity law; systematic administrative boundary bias observed across district and state levels; persistent urban-rural division over 20 years
comments: Network clustering reveals unexpected systematicity in Austrian migration; gravity models systematically overpredict cross-boundary flows; methodology applicable to other countries.

model_io.model: Inferential network clustering + gravity model comparison

hypotheses.hypothesis: Internal migration exhibits systematic administrative bias not captured by gravity models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by observed reduction in cross-boundary flows and regionalization patterns

title: Interpretable spatio-temporal graph neural networks for air quality prediction under real-world multi-station monitoring data
task: Spatio-temporal air quality forecasting via graph attention and interpretable feature importance
key_results: R² = 93.23%, RMSE = 21.66 μg/m³, MAE = 12.08 μg/m³; feature attention mechanism provides interpretable variable importance correlated with domain knowledge
comments: CIST-GNN captures both spatial (GAT) and temporal (GRU) dependencies; interpretability mechanism aids decision-making but evaluation limited to single city (Beijing).

inputs: pollutant concentrations (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, SO2, O3)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spatial graph structure improves forecasting over temporal-only models (GRU)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CIST-GNN outperforms GRU baseline and addresses spatial dependencies

title: An adaptive neuro-fuzzy blockchain–AI framework for secure and intelligent FinTech transactions
task: Fraud detection in FinTech via blockchain-aware neuro-fuzzy AI
key_results: Functional feasibility demonstrated; blockchain-integrity feedback contributes to risk-sensitive detection in proof-of-concept
comments: Integrates blockchain as active decision component rather than passive storage; limited to five-node consortium; real-world validation needed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Coupling blockchain-integrity metrics with machine-learning risk improves fraud detection specificity
hypotheses.result: Supported in controlled proof-of-concept; requires institutional data for confirmation

title: Risk-aware multiple-choice question answering with conformal P-values
task: Risk-aware MCQA via conformal prediction sets with differential privacy
key_results: Empirical miscoverage at α=0.05: 0.0390–0.0399 (MMLU), 0.0469–0.0487 (MMLU-Pro); sets contract smoothly with risk tolerance; conformal p-values provide interpretable rankings
comments: Conformal prediction ensures finite-sample coverage guarantees; practical interface for users to control ambiguity; no privacy overhead reported in abstract.

model_io.model: Conformal prediction on instruction-tuned LLMs (5 models tested)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Conformal prediction sets achieve target miscoverage rate across diverse LLMs and question subsets
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; empirical miscoverage within expected range across 100 calibration–test splits

title: Parity-aligned control allocation for stochastic aeroelastic systems with distributed actuation
task: Control allocation for stochastic aeroelastic systems via parity-aligned symmetry decomposition
key_results: Parity-aligned allocation reproduces full-space response to numerical roundoff; residual-covariance spectral contraction condition enables tail-risk reduction; 24 distributed actuators validated
comments: Novel symmetry-structured framework avoids incorrect antisymmetric-mode vanishment; nonlinear stress-tests show residual scales increase under perturbation, limiting tail-risk claims.

model_io.model: Parity-aligned control allocation with block-preconditioned feasibility correction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Equivariance-based decomposition yields identical residual loads and actuator utilization as full-space damped-pseudoinverse
hypotheses.result: Confirmed to numerical roundoff in nominal case; breaks down under nonlinear perturbation

title: Adaptive federated edge intelligence with semantic communication and trust-aware optimization for heterogeneous IoT networks
task: Federated learning for heterogeneous IoT with semantic communication
key_results: 91.2% accuracy at 5 dB SNR, 120 training rounds, 38% communication overhead reduction
comments: Addresses non-IID data and device heterogeneity simultaneously; practical integration of semantics into federated averaging is novel but evaluated only in simulation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Joint optimization of semantic representation and resource allocation outperforms independent optimization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via 38% overhead reduction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive client participation improves resilience under intermittent connectivity
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated in simulation with reliable aggregation under temporary link failures

title: Comparative predictive modelling of machine learning techniques for network traffic analysis
task: Network traffic prediction via comparative ensemble regression modeling
key_results: XGBoost R² = 0.9969, LightGBM R² = 0.9957, ensemble R² = 0.9965; ensemble weights 47.5% each for XGBoost and LightGBM; UNSW-NB15 reframed as regression
comments: Reformulates intrusion detection dataset as continuous traffic metric prediction; ensemble achieves stability of individual best model; generalization to real traffic flows not validated.

model_io.model: SVR, RFR, XGBoost, LightGBM, MLP regression + weighted ensemble
inputs: UNSW-NB15 network flow features (transformed to continuous metric)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ensemble averaging XGBoost and LightGBM preserves best-model performance with improved robustness
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ensemble R² = 0.9965 competitive with single best (0.9969)

title: Driver activity detection and classification using deep learning-based YOLO models for intelligent transportation systems
task: Driver activity detection via YOLO object detection for intelligent transportation systems
key_results: YOLOv8n achieves 96.0% precision, 95.2% recall, 96.3% mAP@0.5 on 5,422 images; consistent improvement with model complexity; 8 activity classes detected
comments: Transfer learning on YOLOv5/v8 variants shows monotonic performance gains; strong results but evaluation limited to single dataset collected under natural conditions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model complexity correlates with detection performance for multi-class driver activity recognition
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; YOLOv8n outperforms smaller variants by 6% mAP@0.5

title: A tailings dam safety question answering framework integrating a knowledge graph with retrieval augmented generation
task: Domain-specific QA for tailings dam safety via knowledge graph and retrieval-augmented generation
key_results: Intent recognition F1 = 94.12%; RAGAS answer relevancy 0.89, faithfulness 0.82, context precision 0.87; KG: 21 entity types, 2,911 entities, 20,146 relations
comments: Integrates structured KG with fine-tuned LLM via LoRA; strong performance on 2,346 held-out QA pairs; scalability and real-world deployment remain open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structured KG + RAG improves domain relevance and evidence grounding vs. standalone LLM
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated by high RAGAS faithfulness and context precision scores

title: RBDYOLO improves small object detection in low altitude remote sensing imagery
task: Small object detection in UAV imagery via adaptive receptive-field reweighting
key_results: 49.6% precision, 39.4% recall, 40.1% mAP@0.5 (VisDrone); outperforms YOLOv11n baseline by 5.2 mAP@0.5 points; 3.47 M parameters
comments: RBD-YOLO addresses scale mismatch through three coordinated mechanisms; auxiliary cross-dataset validation shows competitive performance on vehicle-centric tasks.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Learnable cross-scale fusion (method B) provides dominant accuracy gain for scale diversity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by ablation; method B attributed largest increment

title: A machine learning framework for privacy preserving personalized multimodal emotion recognition
task: Privacy-preserving personalized multimodal emotion recognition via federated meta-learning and differential privacy
key_results: 4.1% accuracy improvement over centralized models; 95.8% of federated performance at ε=3.0; 14.7% personalization gain with 5 adaptation steps; 86.3% performance with incomplete modalities
comments: P3MER reconciles accuracy, privacy, and personalization; meta-learning enables rapid per-user adaptation; formal (ε,δ)-DP guarantees provided; evaluated on three benchmark datasets with heterogeneous modalities.

model_io.model: Federated meta-learning + hierarchical multimodal fusion + differential privacy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Federated meta-learning enables rapid personalization (≥78% gain, 20–50 samples) while maintaining formal privacy guarantees

hypotheses.hypothesis: Privacy-preserving training achieves higher accuracy than centralized baselines due to personalization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 4.1% improvement over state-of-the-art centralized models

title: A label-free adaptive signal reconstruction strategy within a supervised framework for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
task: Rolling bearing fault diagnosis with label-free VMD optimization
key_results: 99.75% ± 0.22% (CWRU), 99.88% ± 0.10% (Paderborn) accuracy; label-free parameter selection via improved porcupine optimizer
comments: Avoids manual modal selection; high accuracy on fixed-load benchmarks but generalization to variable-load conditions untested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Composite IMF selection index outperforms single-criterion modal screening

key_results: 94.2% mean detection accuracy, 35 ms avg. inference time per frame, monocular vision + GAN augmentation replaces depth sensors, 900 annotated images in diverse conditions
comments: Perception-calibration-control coupling is novel integration; edge deployment enables real-time closed-loop manipulation; scalability claimed but not validated on multiple production lines.

title: Exponential measurement error mitigation in quantum sampling
task: Exponential measurement error mitigation in quantum sampling via majority-vote repetition codes
key_results: Measurement errors suppressed by orders of magnitude with modest linear qubit overhead; exponential suppression persists under realistic gate imperfections; applicable to measurement-based quantum computation and random circuit sampling
comments: Simple repetition-based scheme scales well; hardware-compatible encoding prior to readout; experimental validation on superconducting platforms; practical approach for near-term quantum devices.

model_io.model: Repetition-code majority-vote decoder with encoding robustness

hypotheses.hypothesis: Repetition encoding + majority voting achieves exponential error suppression despite realistic gate imperfections

title: Multi agent PPO for terahertz cell free mobile edge computing networks
task: Multi-agent task offloading and resource allocation in THz cell-free MEC networks
key_results: MAPPO achieves stable convergence and outperforms MADDPG and MATD3 baselines; superior performance vs. conventional cellular and small-cell systems
comments: MAPPO with Beta/Dirichlet action space parameterization enforces physical constraints; Metaverse application context motivates latency-energy tradeoff; specific quantitative metrics not provided in abstract.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MAPPO architecture with constrained action space outperforms MADDPG/MATD3 on NP-hard resource allocation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by convergence and performance comparisons vs. baselines

title: Distinct lattice and charge excitations in AV3Sb5 kagome superconductors
task: Characterize distinct lattice and charge excitations in AV₃Sb₅ kagome superconductors
key_results: E2g phonon twofold-degeneracy lifting (3 GHz splitting) observed in all three compounds (Cs, Rb, K); collective CDW excitations show material-dependent polarization dependences; provides insight into symmetry breaking mechanisms
comments: Polarized Raman spectroscopy combined with DFT and effective model provides complementary views; the material dependence despite identical lattice structure suggests alkali-metal affects electronic interactions subtly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: E2g phonon mode degeneracy lifting occurs in all AV₃Sb₅ compounds in CDW phase
hypotheses.result: Confirmed (previously known only for CsV₃Sb₅)

hypotheses.hypothesis: CDW excitations show material-dependent behavior despite identical normal-state lattice
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; alkali-metal species affects CDW collective mode properties

title: Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator
task: Achieve optical control of electrons in Floquet topological insulator using circularly polarized light
key_results: Demonstrated photocurrent circular dichroism, all-optical anomalous Hall effect, and valley-polarized currents in light-dressed graphene; observed subcycle phase sensitivity enabling ultrafast control
comments: Harmonic Floquet spectroscopy is a sophisticated technique requiring phase-locked fields; practical scalability to room temperature and device integration remains unclear.

inputs: femtosecond laser pulses 1550 nm circular polarization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phase-locked harmonic field enables dynamic control of electrons in Floquet topological bands
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; subcycle phase sensitivity observed

title: Symmetric tilt grain boundaries in uranium nitride and uranium carbide
task: Characterize symmetric tilt grain boundaries in uranium nitride and uranium carbide using DFT
key_results: Σ03 (111)[1̄10] GB most stable in both UN and UC; GB energy global minimum at 70° tilt angle; strong parabolic correlation between excess volume and GB energy for UN; stacking fault energy values obtained; results consistent with rock-salt MgO reference
comments: DFT study provides good baseline for equilibrium microstructure, but kinetic barriers for GB formation and migration are not addressed.

inputs: 14 symmetric tilt grain boundary configurations (UN and UC)

hypotheses.hypothesis: GB energy has global minimum at specific tilt angle independent of material
hypotheses.result: Confirmed at 70° tilt for both UN and UC

hypotheses.hypothesis: Excess volume is good predictor of GB energy in UN
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; strong parabolic correlation observed

title: Using the clean portion of a CHIRP pulse to determine the time of arrival of a hydroacoustic signal under strong reflection conditions
task: Improve time-of-arrival estimation for hydroacoustic signals under multipath reflection
key_results: Using initial clean pulse segment reduced mean absolute error from 20.7 µs to 2.7 µs (range 2 m) and 175.6 µs to 3.1 µs (range 4 m); achieved 100% detection within ±20 µs tolerance; 1.7 µs error at 4 m with 2 ms pulse
comments: The method is simple and practical but effectiveness depends on pulse duration and reflection strength; gains diminish if reflection onset is very early.

model_io.model: CHIRP pulse analysis with multipath simulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Restricting analysis to initial pulse segment improves ToA accuracy under strong multipath conditions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with 6-100× error reduction depending on configuration

title: A bilayer model for magnetic stimulation of neural tissue using a micro dual-coil system
task: Optimize magnetic field orientation for neural tissue stimulation using micro coils
key_results: 180° phase-shifted dual-coil system generates stronger and more uniform magnetic field than single or in-phase dual-coil configurations; induced current can be aligned with axon axis via phase/amplitude adjustment
comments: The bilayer model simplification may not capture all tissue heterogeneity, but admittance lattice discretization provides a computationally tractable approach.

model_io.model: Pseudo-3D bilayer model + admittance lattice discretization

hypotheses.hypothesis: 180° phase-shifted dual-coil produces stronger/more uniform field than in-phase configuration
hypotheses.result: Confirmed

title: Toward next-generation computing through ferroelectricity
task: Review ferroelectric materials for next-generation computing and memory applications
key_results: Ferroelectric thin films enable electrically switchable, non-volatile polarization for integrated memory-computation; polarization engineering controls charge transport, interfacial barriers, and conductance; design principles for scalable, energy-efficient devices outlined
comments: This is a review article synthesizing existing knowledge; concrete quantitative breakthroughs are not detailed in the abstract, limiting assessment of specific performance metrics.
